title: Oma Said Breathe (Chas McIvor)
style: acoustic folk fingerpicked guitar warm baritone male vocal 96bpm gentle brushed drums generational family portrait true story grandmother wisdom unhurried intimate
lyrics:
[Intro - acoustic guitar, warm and gentle, old-timey feel]
Oma said it.
To Joel.
When he was singing.
Nay Joel.
You have to breathe when you sing.

[Verse 1]
He was trying
He just couldn't
The left side had always been wrong
The cartilage, the passage, the whole arrangement
He was singing and not breathing
Because breathing wasn't working
And Oma watched him try
And said the one thing
That was technically correct
But physically impossible
At the time

[Verse 2]
Years later
He got the nose fixed
The camera went up
The left side confirmed
The other side not much better
Silver Chain came every morning for the dressing
After the operation
And he texted:
Hopefully be able to breathe again
And: Oma said breathe when you sing
Trust me I was trying

[Chorus]
Oma said breathe
Joel was trying
Oma said breathe
He just couldn't
Oma said breathe
The nose wasn't right
Oma said breathe
He got it fixed
Oma said breathe
Now he can
Oma said breathe
And Ari already knows
She never had that problem
She breathes and the room holds still
Oma said breathe

[Bridge - spoken, warm and generational]
Oma coached Joel on singing.
Joel coaches Ari just by watching.
Ari sings in front of her dad's mate with a head cold
and the man who ran venues
says: wow.
The breathing sorted itself out across generations.
Oma would be pleased.
She always knew what was needed.
She just said it early.
Which is when you should.

[Outro - guitar alone, fading gently]
Nay Joel
You have to breathe
When you sing
He was trying
He just couldn't
Now he can
Oma
Was right
